summary: A Robotbox.net review by Richard Harrison comparing the iRobot Roomba J7 and Roomba J7+ robot vacuums, released in September 2021 and reviewed June 2023. The note concludes the two models are nearly identical in performance, with the main difference being that the J7+ includes the CleanBase self-emptying unit and dirt disposal bags. It covers design, cleaning performance, test results, battery and runtime, navigation, smart features, and includes reader comments and Amazon price listings.
one_line: Robotbox review comparing the iRobot Roomba J7 and J7+ vacuums, which differ mainly in the included CleanBase self-emptying unit.
key_facts: The Roomba J7 and Roomba J7+ were released in September 2021 as part of the Roomba J Series.
The Roomba J7+ includes the iRobot CleanBase unit and disposable bags, enabling automatic self-emptying, while the Roomba J7 does not include the CleanBase unit.
Both the Roomba J7 and J7+ have a 1700 Pa power suction rating and a 0.3L dustbin capacity in the comparison table.
The article states the Roomba J7 and J7+ both have a 13.3-inch diameter, stand 3.4 inches tall, and weigh 7.49 lbs.
Both models use a 2210 mAh Roomba i8 Denali battery that the article says offers a 90-minute runtime, though the comparison table lists 100 minutes.
AeroForce high-efficiency filters are said to capture 99.9% of allergens, dust, dust mite, and other particles.
Both models sync with the Braava M6 mop via Imprint Link technology for simultaneous vacuuming and mopping.
The J7 and J7+ use VSLAM navigation called iAdapt 3.0 with Imprint Smart Mapping and a front-facing camera.
The J7 has PrecisionVision Navigation that can identify common obstacles such as socks, shoes, power cords, and dog poop.
The J7 features Quiet Drive, which turns the motor off when moving from the dock to the target location, a feature the article says iRobot borrowed from Neato.
The article recommends the Roomba J7 for buyers on a budget who are willing to empty the bin manually, and the J7+ for those who want a self-emptying robot.
The Roomba J7 uses a 2.4GHz WiFi connection and is controlled through the iRobot Home app, and is powered by iRobot Genius 3.0.
The recharge time for the J series is listed as 2-3 hours in the review text and 3-4 hours in the comparison table.
In reader comments, Swartzcop Kennedy estimated the Roomba J7+ runs about 45 minutes to one and a half hours per charge and recharges in about an hour.
